prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: remortgaging at the end of a fixed rate. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the fixed rate is ending within the next 3 to 6 months, I check the likely reversion rate early so I can tell whether a simple product switch or a full remortgage is the better fit."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the current lender offers a retention deal, I compare the total cost over the new term rather than focusing on the headline rate alone, because fees and incentives can change the answer."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member says they want to stay put, I prefer to confirm whether a new deal can be arranged without changing the loan amount, term or borrowing purpose, as that usually makes the case simpler."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the fixed rate is ending and the member has had a change in income, I revisit affordability rather than assuming the original assessment still holds, especially if they want to borrow more."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member is switching lender, I always check for early repayment charges on the existing deal, because those can outweigh a slightly better new rate."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the property value has moved since completion, I use the current loan-to-value position to judge whether remortgaging could unlock a better rate band."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member is close to the end of their fixed term, I prefer to gather paperwork early, including the latest statement and income evidence if needed, so the new offer does not run out before completion."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the purpose is mainly to avoid moving onto the standard variable rate, I focus on timing first, because a delay of even a few weeks can add avoidable cost."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there is an interest-only element, I make sure the repayment strategy still works at remortgage, since a new lender may review that more closely than the existing one."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member wants to remortgage and borrow extra for home improvements, I separate the rate switch from the additional borrowing conversation, because that helps me test affordability and risk more clearly."}]}
